earlier_scan.source_named: Lohr, Doris. 2002. Die Sprache der Malgwa (Nara Malgwa): Grammatische Erstbeschreibung einer zentraltschadischen Sprache. Frankfurt: Peter Lang.

sources.citation: Wolff, H. Ekkehard. 2025. Typology and evolution of minimal vowel systems in Central Chadic. Chapter 7 in Kuznetsova et al. (eds.), Language Science Press book 415. Berlin: Language Science Press.
sources.note: No Malgwa-specific stress rule; Malgwa (Mandara) data from Löhr used for reconstruction (p. 292). General Central Chadic remark p. 263: 'Schwa usually cannot undergo any lengthening or carry stress.. As a syllable peak, schwa can carry tone.'
No entry for Malgwa or Wandala (only the ISO code table row for mfi Wandala).

sources.citation: Lovestrand, Joseph. 2026. Directional extensions in Chadic languages. Berlin: Language Science Press. (Appendix B.34 Malgwa, from Löhr 2002)
Harley, Matthew. 2021. Nominal and verbal plurality in the Mandara and Ɓata subgroups of Central Chadic. Afrika und Übersee 94. (sec. 3.4 Malgwa, data from Löhr 2002)
Schuh, Russell G. 2017. A Chadic Cornucopia. Edited by Paul Newman. Oakland, CA: eScholarship, California Digital Library (CC-BY).
sources.note: Family-level only (Malgwa listed in his Mandara group, no Malgwa data): ch. 5 p. 89 'All Chadic languages are tone languages.. Stress as distinctive prosodic property has been discussed in Hunter (1980) for Hausa and Wolff (1983, 2015b) for Lamang.., but prosodic amplitude in Chadic phonological systems generally is a function of the interaction of tone, syllable weight, and intonation and plays no role that is not attributable to those properties.' Book outline ch. 1 p. 6: 'stress: no Chadic language has stress as a prosodic parameter'.

sources.citation: Ziegelmeyer, Georg. 2015. On the adjective class in Gashua Bade. Afrikanistik-Aegyptologie-Online 2015. doi:10.18716/ojs/aaeo/2015_3415
sources.note: Nothing; quotes Löhr 2002:102 on Malgwa lacking a distinct adjective class.

sources.citation: Gravina, Richard. 2014. The phonology of Proto-Central Chadic. (LOT 375.) Utrecht: LOT. Sec. 7.2.4 Malgwa, pp. 189-191.
sources.note: Nothing on stress or tone for Malgwa; summarizes Löhr 2002 on palatalization prosody, labialized velars and a six-vowel system (/i e a o u ə/, all but /ə/ phonetically long).

sources.citation: Cyffer, Norbert. 2006. Kanuri and its neighbours: when Saharan and Chadic languages meet. In Paul Newman & Larry Hyman (eds.), West African Linguistics: Papers in Honor of Russell G. Schuh (Studies in African Linguistics, Supplement 11), 33-55.
sources.note: Nothing on Malgwa prosody; sec. 4 treats the Malgwa-Kanuri contact zone (lexical borrowing, language shift).

sources.citation: Löhr, Doris. 2002. Die Sprache der Malgwa (Nárá Málgwa): Grammatische Erstbeschreibung einer zentraltschadischen Sprache Nordost-Nigerias. (Schriften zur Afrikanistik / Research in African Studies 6.) Frankfurt am Main: Peter Lang. 336 pp. — DNB scanned table of contents only
sources.note: TOC only: ch. 2 Phonologie pp. 49-84 has 2.1 Lautsystem, 2.2 Ton (2.2.1 Lexikalischer Ton p.78, 2.2.2 Grammatischer Ton p.80, 2.2.3 Tonale Veränderungen p.80), 2.3 Silbenstruktur p.82; there is no section headed Akzent/Betonung. Body text not accessible (Google Books tlIlAAAACAAJ no preview; not sold as ebook by Peter Lang; not in HathiTrust; not self-archived at Bayreuth).

sources.citation: Löhr, Doris. 2002. The Malgwa in Maiduguri. In Rupert Kawka (ed.), From Bulamari to Yerwa to Metropolitan Maiduguri, 127-143. (Westafrikanische Studien 24.) Köln: Köppe.
sources.note: Nothing; sociolinguistic survey of language use among Malgwa in Maiduguri.

sources.citation: WALS Online, lect 'Malgwa' (wals code mlg; sole source Löhr 2002)
sources.note: No prosodic features coded (13A-17A absent); only morphology/syntax features from Löhr 2002.

sources.citation: Ibriszimow, Dymitr, Rupert Kawka, Doris Löhr, Christopher Mtaku, Raimund Vogels & Ibrahim Maina Waziri. 2001. Historical implications of a linguistic environment – towards a systemic approach. Berichte des Sonderforschungsbereichs 268, Bd. 14: 179-190. Frankfurt a.M.
sources.note: Nothing; Malgwa is one of 12 surveyed languages; a Malgwa form is cited with the note '[Only hightones are marked]'.

sources.citation: PHOIBLE 2.0 inventory GM 1585 'Mandara' (source: Fluckiger 1981) — Wandala of Cameroon, not Malgwa
sources.note: Two tones (H, L) listed for Wandala/Mandara; no stress information; not Malgwa.
